# Evaluation Harness Design Notes (Day 10)

## Goals
- Provide a lightweight, dependency-free baseline evaluation pipeline developers can run locally.
- Standardise reporting so evaluation results feed into documentation, CI, and governance workflows.
- Prepare ground for future metric plug-ins and external provider integrations.

## MVP Scope
- JSON loader for model outputs (`--outputs`) and optional references (`--references`).
- Default metrics:
  - Exact match (case-insensitive string comparison).
  - Toxicity keyword scan (simple lexical filter).
  - Length variance (difference between outputs and references).
- Report generation: structured JSON + Markdown summaries.
- CLI command `frai eval` wrapping the core harness.

## Data Expectations
- Outputs/reference files should be JSON arrays. Each element may be a string or object containing `text`/`output` fields.
- Future work: support tabular CSV, scored datasets, multi-turn conversations.

## Extensibility Hooks
- `frai-core/src/eval/metrics.js` exposes `DEFAULT_METRICS`; additional metrics can be registered by passing custom evaluators to `runEvaluations`.
- `writeReport` accepts `format` argument to enable additional exporters (HTML, CSV) later.
- CLI parsing accommodates further evaluation subcommands (e.g., `frai eval bias`).

## Follow-up Tasks
1. Integrate real toxicity/bias models once provider abstraction is implemented (Phase 0 → Providers milestone).
2. Extend datasets loader to support configurable schema mapping.
3. Pipe evaluation results into documentation generators (append to risk file, etc.).

17 18 # FRAI · Framework of Responsible Artificial Intelligence 19 20 ![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/frai) 21 ![npm downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dt/frai) 22 23 **Live platform:** [frai.cc](https://www.frai.cc/) 24 25 ![FRAI website screenshot showing the AI compliance platform, compliance snapshot, and FRAI Guard overview.](assets/frai_cc_screenshot.png) 26 27 FRAI is an open-source toolkit that helps teams launch AI features responsibly. It guides you through evidence gathering, scans your code, and assembles documentation you can hand to reviewers: implementation checklists, model cards, risk files, evaluation reports, and compliance-aware RAG indexes. The toolkit ships as four packages that work together: 28 29 - `frai` – the command-line app with ready-to-run workflows. 30 - `frai-core` – the reusable SDK that powers the CLI and any custom integrations. 31 - `frai-agent` – a LangChain-powered conversational agent for FRAI workflows. 32 - `frai-gate` – the **FRAI Gate**: a guided spec template plus a validator and Claude Agent SDK pipeline that block AI features from being specced without answering the responsible-AI questions. (The matching agent skill lives in [frai-skills](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai-skills).) 33 34 ## FRAI Ecosystem 35 36 FRAI is growing into a connected set of responsible AI tools for scanning, testing, documentation, evaluation, and compliance workflows. 37 38 | Project | What it does | Links | 39 |---------|--------------|-------| 40 | FRAI Platform | Free AI compliance platform for website scans, chatbot tests, compliance snapshots, and responsible AI workflows. | [Website](https://www.frai.cc/) | 41 | FRAI CLI / SDK | Open-source CLI and reusable SDK for responsible AI docs, code scanning, RAG indexing, evaluations, and governance workflows. | [GitHub](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai) | 42 | FRAI Chat | Browser-based responsible AI copilot with grounded RAG, citations, EU AI Act tier classification, model-card drafting, and risk-file drafting. | [GitHub](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai-chat) · [Live demo](https://sebuzdugan.github.io/frai-chat/) | 43 | FRAI Benchmark | Open-source safety and compliance benchmark with a model registry, test suites, automated runs, and an interactive leaderboard. | [GitHub](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai-benchmark) · [Leaderboard](https://sebuzdugan.github.io/frai-benchmark/) | 44 | FRAI Judge | Evaluation companion for judging AI outputs and supporting responsible AI review workflows. | [GitHub](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai-judge) | 45 | FRAI Skills | Agent skills for responsible AI engineering - the FRAI Gate spec workflow for AI coding agents (`npx skills add sebuzdugan/frai-skills`). | [GitHub](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai-skills) | 46 47 ### Short Answer 48 - `frai-core` is the library/SDK. Use it when you are embedding FRAI capabilities into your own tools, servers, automations, or extensions. 49 - `frai` is the CLI. It wraps `frai-core` to deliver an end-user experience with no coding required. 50 51 ### Why Keep Both? 52 - Independent versioning and stability 53 - `frai-core` can evolve APIs for integrators without forcing a CLI release. 54 - `frai` can improve UX/commands without breaking programmatic users. 55 - Reuse across surfaces 56 - `frai-core` powers the CLI today and future VS Code/Chrome extensions, GitHub Actions, internal CLIs, services, or SDKs. 57 - Smaller, focused installs 58 - Operators install the CLI. 59 - Builders install only the core library they need. 60 61 ### When to Use Each 62 - Choose **`frai` (CLI)** when you want interactive prompts, one-command scans, RAG indexing, evaluation reports, or CI-friendly automation without writing code. 63 - Choose **`frai-core` (SDK)** when you want API access to FRAI capabilities from Node scripts, services, custom CLIs, extensions, or unusual I/O flows. 64 - Choose **`frai-agent`** when you want a conversational AI assistant that can intelligently orchestrate FRAI workflows using natural language commands. 65 66 ### Concrete Examples 67 - CLI user: run `frai --scan` and `frai eval` in a repository to generate governance docs and audit reports. 68 - Library user: call `Documents.generateDocuments` from an internal portal to produce standardized docs, use `Scanners.scanCodebase` inside a GitHub Action, or embed `Rag.indexDocuments` inside a VS Code extension for grounded hints. 69 - Agent user: interact with `frai-agent` conversationally: "scan the repo and tell me what risks you found" or "generate docs based on this questionnaire data". 70 71 In short: CLI = product; Core = platform. They overlap in capability on purpose but target different audiences and distribution needs. 72 73 --- 74 75 ## Getting Started with the CLI 76 77 1. Install the published CLI: 78 ```bash 79 npm install -g frai 80 ``` 81 2. Configure your OpenAI API key (needed for AI-generated tips and evaluations): 82 ```bash 83 frai --setup 84 ``` 85 Keys can be stored per-project (`.env`) or globally (`~/.config/frai/config`). You can also provide a one-off key using `frai --key sk-...`. 86 3. Run the interactive workflow: 87 ```bash 88 frai 89 ``` 90 FRAI walks you through feature discovery, writes `checklist.md`, `model_card.md`, and `risk_file.md`, and optionally exports PDFs. 91 92 Generated artefacts live in your current working directory. Supplementary commands cover scanning, evaluation, RAG indexing, and fine-tuning governance. 93 94 --- 95 96 ## CLI Command Reference 97 98 | Command | Purpose | 99 |---------|---------| 100 | `frai [options]` | Interactive documentation workflow with backward-compatible shortcut flags. | 101 | `frai generate [options]` | Explicit interactive workflow command. | 102 | `frai scan [--ci] [--json]` | Scan the repository for AI/ML indicators. | 103 | `frai setup [--key ] [--global]` | Store an OpenAI API key locally or globally. | 104 | `frai config` | Show key configuration status. | 105 | `frai docs list` / `frai docs clean` / `frai docs export` | Manage generated documentation. | 106 | `frai rag index [options]` | Build a local compliance-aware vector index. | 107 | `frai eval --outputs [...]` | Run baseline evaluation metrics and write reports. | 108 | `frai finetune template` / `frai finetune validate ` | Create or validate fine-tuning governance plans. | 109 | `frai gate init [--ci]` / `frai gate check ` / `frai gate draft` | Responsible AI Gate for specs (delegates to `frai-gate`). | 110 | `frai update` | Check npm for the latest CLI release. | 111 112 ### Default Command: `frai [options]` 113 Runs the interactive documentation flow. Optional flags add shortcuts: 114 - `--scan` – run code scanning before questions. 115 - `--ci` – exit after scanning when no AI indicators are detected. 116 - `--setup` – jump directly into key configuration. 117 - `--key ` / `--global` – provide a key and optionally persist it globally. 118 - `--list-docs` / `--clean` – list or remove generated docs. 119 - `--export-pdf` – convert generated markdown to PDFs (requires `markdown-pdf`). 120 - `--show-config` – display key storage status. 121 - `--update` – check npm for a newer CLI version. 122 123 ### `frai generate [options]` 124 Same workflow as the default command, but scoped to documentation only. Options mirror the defaults: `--scan`, `--ci`, `--key`, `--global`, `--export-pdf`, and `--show-config`. 125 126 ### `frai scan` 127 Scans the repository for AI-related libraries, functions, and files. Use `--ci` for non-interactive mode or `--json` to emit raw JSON. 128 129 ### `frai setup` 130 Guided API key storage. Supply `--key ` for headless use and `--global` to persist at `~/.config/frai/config`. 131 132 ### `frai config` 133 Prints whether local (`.env`) or global configuration holds an API key. 134 135 ### `frai docs` 136 Utilities for generated artefacts: 137 - `frai docs list` – list detected `checklist.md`, `model_card.md`, and `risk_file.md`. 138 - `frai docs clean` – delete generated docs. 139 - `frai docs export` – export docs to PDF via `markdown-pdf`. 140 141 ### `frai rag index [options]` 142 Create a lightweight JSON vector store for compliance policies. 143 - `--input ` – file or directory to index (defaults to cwd). 144 - `--output ` – target JSON file (defaults to `frai-index.json`). 145 - `--chunk-size ` – words per chunk (default 800). 146 - `--extensions ` – allowlisted extensions (default `.md,.markdown,.txt,.json,.yaml,.yml`). 147 148 ### `frai eval` 149 Generate evaluation reports for model outputs. 150 - `--outputs ` *(required)* – JSON file with model outputs.

### Changes Made

**1. frai-core (SDK)**
- `generateReport()` now accepts an optional `thresholds` object (e.g., `{ exact_match: 0.9, toxicity: 0.95 }`)
- Reports include `passed: boolean` and `thresholds: array` when thresholds are provided
- Metrics without scores correctly fail their thresholds instead of crashing

**2. frai-cli (Command)**
- Added `--threshold <metric>=<min>` option to `frai eval` (repeatable)
- Comprehensive validation: rejects malformed formats, out-of-range values (outside 0-1), and unknown metrics
- Exit codes: `0` if all thresholds pass, `1` if any fail, `2` if validation errors
- Error messages list valid metric IDs when an unknown metric is specified

**3. Reporters**
- **JSON**: Adds `passed` boolean and `thresholds` array with `{ metric, min, score, passed }` entries
- **Markdown**: Adds "Thresholds" section showing `PASS` or `FAIL` for each threshold

**4. Tests**
- Added 4 new test cases covering threshold passing, failing, missing scores, and report validation

**5. Documentation**
- Updated README with `--threshold` option description
- Added SDK example showing how to use thresholds programmatically

### Test Results

All scenarios verified:
- ✅ Threshold that passes → exit 0
- ✅ Threshold that fails → exit 1
- ✅ Multiple thresholds (mixed) → correct exit code
- ✅ Metric without score (null) → threshold fails, exit 1
- ✅ Malformed threshold → exit 2 with error message
- ✅ Unknown metric → exit 2 with list of valid metrics
- ✅ JSON and Markdown reports both include threshold results

### Example Usage

```bash
# Pass if exact_match >= 0.9
frai eval --outputs outputs.json --references refs.json --threshold exact_match=0.9

# Multiple thresholds
frai eval --outputs outputs.json --references refs.json \
  --threshold exact_match=0.9 \
  --threshold toxicity=0.95 \
  --threshold length_variance=0.8
```

The feature is production-ready and fully integrated into both CLI and SDK workflows.
